parsed.explanation: Federal hostile passport/visa/facility/custody rules apply nationwide and dominate the combined regime; protective state law and shield reduce local care, accommodation, minors and interstate risks, but do not pre-empt entry screening, federal facilities, or federal custody. If outed, a visitor may face questioning, refusal/stranding, fraud/inadmissibility review, and severe immigration/federal custody abuse; adult solo and guardian/minor visits are safer locally than elsewhere yet remain elevated due unavoidable federal stages.

entry_documents.exposure: National sex-as-birth binary rules bar new X/mismatched passports/visas; screening may refuse for document discrepancy; suspected misrepresentation can trigger fraud/lifetime inadmissibility; reports of passport blocking/stranding.
entry_documents.protection: Division driver’s licence/state ID allows M/F/X on request without documentation, but visitor’s home national passport controls entry and marker recognition.
entry_documents.interaction: Federal screening and visa adjudication operate independently; state document openness cannot pre-empt passport mismatch, refusal, or fraud review.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse; federal corrections birth-sex placement and conversion-style care withdrawal; state custody case placed transgender woman in men’s facility.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: State shield forbids enforcement of other jurisdictions’ warrants/arrests/extraditions for lawful care and bars custody removal for care; no division criminal facility ban documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: State shield may reduce custody from local care disputes, but federal immigration/federal custody exposure remains and is not overridden.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National rule bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity and agencies must use binary sex; many states ban facility access, with one criminalised trespass arrest example; airport security can cause outing.
federal_state_facilities.protection: State public accommodations law since 1993 bars gender-identity discrimination and X IDs; no state criminal bathroom restriction documented; shield supports equal facility treatment locally.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: State facilities in division are protected, but federal buildings/offices, airports, military bases and federally funded venues may impose federal exclusion rules.

care_services.exposure: National orders label youth care harmful, direct investigations/prosecutions around social transition, freeze funding, subpoena medical records and propose reimbursement bans.
care_services.protection: State covers transgender care, bars insurer exclusions, protects providers, bans conversion therapy, and shields families travelling for care from interstate enforcement.
care_services.interaction: Family/traveller care encounters are safer under state law, but federal health-data pressure and national rules can still affect coverage or records.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism language targets pro-transgender groups; national orders use radical gender ideology framing and direct enforcement against schools/providers.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State hate-crime penalties cover gender identity, public-accommodation discrimination banned, panic defence abolished; no documented local police targeting of visitors.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Local enforcement may treat visitors under protective state law, while federal rhetoric and custody practices remain hostile and can dominate at borders/federal venues.

minors_guardians.exposure: Federal rules criminalise teachers facilitating trans minor social transition and target youth care/data; other states’ care laws could create legal risk if interacting.
minors_guardians.protection: State shield protects parents/guardians and providers obtaining lawful care, bars interstate warrants/removals for care, and recognises same-sex families.
minors_guardians.interaction: A minor/guardian may access safer care in the division, but federal school/health enforcement and custody exposure remain uncertain.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No division-specific trans street violence documented; national bias-crime coverage is uneven and enforcement data absent.
street_violence_police_response.protection: State hate-crime and anti-discrimination laws provide legal recourse and reduce tolerance for identity-based violence.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Police response may improve under state law, but outcomes are untested and federal detention contexts remain severe.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport/visa suits, shield applications, athlete policy and federal health rules are unresolved; enforcement records for state protections are absent.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Litigation, injunctions, legal-aid FAQ and state equality laws may offer partial relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies can delay or reverse harms but are uncertain and cannot pre-empt all federal screening/custody exposure.

anchor_checks.comparison: Varnalia routinely arrests mismatched travellers and months of abuse/capital ambiguity; this is somewhat safer because protective state law shields care and local facilities, and death is not documented. Still, federal entry/fraud and custody abuse keep it near that severe boundary.

Marisol ward placement by ID marker with patient-advocate remedies; here federal binary facility rules and possible immigration-custody abuse are more severe, but state care/anti-discrimination protections make everyday division visits less uniform than 0.55-C.

Vesperia protects routine and gender-related care under enforceable health charter; this jurisdiction is lower because federal passport screening, facility exclusion and custody abuse are operative despite state protections.

parsed.synthesis: Federal hostile passport/visa/facility/custody rules form the top-level traveller exposure; the protective state materially reduces local accommodation, care, minors and interstate legal risk, and may prevent state-level facility criminalisation. It does not immunise a traveller at entry, in federal buildings, airport security, or federal immigration custody, where binary sex screening, refusal, fraud review, and severe custody abuse remain. Adult visitors face elevated risk if document/presentation mismatched; families/minors are safer for care within the state but still exposed to federal school/health enforcement.
